    inventory: subtract active reservations from stock in the catalogue
---

diff --git a/services/inventory/handlers.py b/services/inventory/handlers.py
index a3b2262..d2b3ca5 100644
--- a/services/inventory/handlers.py
+++ b/services/inventory/handlers.py
@@ -8,7 +8,12 @@ from services.common import db, settings
 
 
 async def list_products() -> list[dict]:
-    rows = await db.fetch("SELECT id, sku, name, price_cents, stock FROM products ORDER BY id")
+    rows = await db.fetch(
+        "SELECT p.id, p.sku, p.name, p.price_cents, "
+        "p.stock - COALESCE((SELECT sum(r.quantity) FROM reservations r "
+        "WHERE r.product_id = p.id AND NOT r.released), 0) AS stock "
+        "FROM products p ORDER BY p.id"
+    )
     return [dict(r) for r in rows]

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit d3672c0 changed inventory list_products to subtract active reservations using a correlated subquery on reservations filtered by product_id and released. The reservations table has about 140k rows and its only index is the primary key on order_id, so there is no index on product_id. Each catalogue request therefore scans the table, and GET /products on inventory now takes about 0.8-0.9 s, which makes shop's calls slow.
evidence: Commit d3672c0 was deployed at 13:54:32, just before the alert at 13:57:57. It adds a correlated subquery over reservations (WHERE r.product_id = p.id AND NOT r.released) to the inventory catalogue query.
The inventory p95 latency rose from 0.005 s to 0.955 s. The shop to inventory upstream p95 shows the same rise (0.0048 s to 0.955 s).
Inventory logs show GET /products at 786 ms and GET /products/9 at 904 ms. POST /reservations takes about 2 ms, so only the catalogue path is slow.
pg_indexes shows reservations only has reservations_pkey on (order_id), with no index on product_id. pg_stat_user_tables shows reservations has 140,130 live rows against only 10 products.
Shop POST /orders now takes about 1018 ms, which is consistent with the slow inventory calls.

The remaining errors are background noise. The shop 5xx rate has fallen against the earlier baseline. The name-resolution and Redis connection errors date from earlier (13:41-13:45), so they predate this change.
The other recent commits do not match the symptom. 9c8441c raises the users DB pool from 10 to 12 and users latency is normal. 03d624c on payments dates from 13:05.
plan: Roll back d3672c0 to restore the plain products query.
Check that the inventory p95 latency and shop POST /orders duration return to baseline (about 5 ms for inventory).
Before re-applying the feature, add an index on reservations(product_id) (ideally partial, WHERE NOT released), or compute reserved quantities with a single grouped aggregate join.
Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the new query against production-sized data before redeploying.

action.reason: This commit introduced an unindexed correlated subquery on the 140k-row reservations table, which slows the inventory catalogue endpoint. Reverting it removes the extra latency.
evidence: The inventory p95 latency rose to 0.955 s after the 13:54:32 deploy.
GET /products takes about 800-900 ms, while the other inventory endpoints take about 2 ms.
reservations has no index on product_id and about 140k rows.
